agentic_ai.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration Patterns
agentic_ai.rationale: Multi-agent systems (planner/builder/judge style pipelines, supervisor-worker graphs) are becoming the default way to scale agentic AI beyond a single monolithic prompt loop.
key_facts: Common topologies: supervisor-worker, peer-to-peer, and pipeline (sequential handoff).
Shared state/message-passing design determines how failures in one agent propagate.
Orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen) differ mainly in how they model control flow.
agentic_ai.exercise_idea: Build a two-agent pipeline (researcher + summarizer) with an explicit handoff contract and a failure fallback.

agentic_ai.title: Tool-Use and Function-Calling Design
agentic_ai.rationale: Well-designed tool schemas are the single biggest lever on agent reliability — vague tool contracts cause silent failures more often than model reasoning gaps.
key_facts: Tool descriptions should specify preconditions, side effects, and failure modes explicitly.
Narrow, single-purpose tools outperform large multi-purpose ones for reliability.
Structured output (JSON schema) validation catches most tool-call errors before execution.
agentic_ai.exercise_idea: Design and implement a small tool schema with explicit error contracts, then test it against three deliberately malformed calls.

agentic_ai.title: Agent Memory and Context Engineering
agentic_ai.rationale: As agent tasks grow longer, what an agent remembers (and forgets) between steps matters more than raw context window size.
key_facts: Short-term (scratchpad) memory and long-term (retrieval-backed) memory solve different problems.
Summarization and compaction strategies trade recall for context budget.
Poor memory design is a leading cause of agents repeating failed actions.
agentic_ai.exercise_idea: Implement a simple rolling-summary memory buffer and measure how it changes a multi-step agent's success rate on a repeated task.

agentic_ai.title: Evaluation and Guardrails for Autonomous Agents
agentic_ai.rationale: Agents that take real-world actions need measurable evaluation and hard guardrails, not just spot-checked demos.
key_facts: LLM-as-judge evaluation needs its own calibration, not blind trust.
Guardrails should be enforced in code (allow-lists, confirmation steps), not just prompted for.
Regression suites for agent behavior catch prompt-change breakage that unit tests miss.
agentic_ai.exercise_idea: Write a small eval harness that scores an agent's tool-call transcript against a rubric and flags guardrail violations.

agentic_ai.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol) Servers
agentic_ai.rationale: MCP standardizes how agents discover and call external tools/data sources, replacing bespoke per-agent integration code.
key_facts: An MCP server exposes tools/resources over a standard protocol any compliant client can call.
This decouples tool implementation from any single agent framework.
Local MCP servers are a practical way to give an agent filesystem/API access safely.
agentic_ai.exercise_idea: Stand up a minimal MCP server exposing one custom tool and connect it to an MCP-compatible client.

cloud_computing.title: Serverless Inference with AWS Lambda and Bedrock
cloud_computing.rationale: Serverless inference removes idle-GPU cost for spiky AI workloads, at the price of cold-start latency you have to design around.
key_facts: AWS Bedrock exposes foundation models behind a managed API with no infrastructure to provision.
Lambda cold starts are the main latency risk for request-driven inference paths.
Provisioned concurrency trades cost for predictable latency.
cloud_computing.exercise_idea: Deploy a Lambda function that calls Bedrock for a single inference request and measure cold-start vs. warm-start latency.

cloud_computing.title: GPU and Accelerator Provisioning and Cost Optimization
cloud_computing.rationale: GPU spend is usually the largest line item in an AI workload's cloud bill, and most of it is avoidable idle time.
key_facts: Spot/preemptible GPU instances can cut cost 60-90% for fault-tolerant batch jobs.
Right-sizing (matching accelerator type to model size) is often more impactful than instance discounts.
Autoscaling GPU pools needs a warm-pool strategy to avoid provisioning-latency penalties.
cloud_computing.exercise_idea: Estimate and compare on-demand vs. spot GPU cost for a small batch inference job, then implement the spot version with a checkpoint/retry strategy.

cloud_computing.title: Vector Databases and RAG Infrastructure
cloud_computing.rationale: Retrieval-augmented generation is the most common way to ground LLM output in your own data, and the vector store is its critical-path dependency.
key_facts: Approximate nearest-neighbor indexes (HNSW, IVF) trade recall for query speed.
Chunking strategy affects retrieval quality more than embedding-model choice in most cases.
Hybrid (keyword + vector) search often outperforms pure vector search for factual queries.
cloud_computing.exercise_idea: Stand up a local vector store, ingest a small document set with two chunking strategies, and compare retrieval quality.

cloud_computing.title: Event-Driven Data Pipelines for LLM Workloads
cloud_computing.rationale: LLM pipelines increasingly need to react to events (new document, user action) rather than run on a fixed batch schedule.
key_facts: Event-driven pipelines decouple producers (data sources) from consumers (embedding/inference jobs) via a queue or stream.
At-least-once delivery semantics mean downstream steps must be idempotent.
Dead-letter queues are essential for isolating malformed events without blocking the pipeline.
cloud_computing.exercise_idea: Build a small event-driven pipeline (queue -> embedding step -> vector store write) and verify idempotent handling of a duplicated event.

cloud_computing.title: Infrastructure as Code for Agent Deployments
cloud_computing.rationale: Agent systems have more moving parts (tool servers, vector stores, queues) than a typical API, making IaC the difference between reproducible and unmanageable deployments.
key_facts: Declarative IaC tools (Terraform, CDK) make agent-infrastructure changes reviewable and revertible.
Environment parity (dev/staging/prod) matters more for agent systems because tool availability differs by environment.
Secrets should be provisioned via the IaC tool's secret-manager integration, never inlined in config.
cloud_computing.exercise_idea: Write an IaC module that provisions one small piece of agent infrastructure (e.g. a queue and a function) and apply it to a sandbox environment.

quantum_computing.title: Hands-On Circuits with Qiskit and Cirq
quantum_computing.rationale: Building and running a real circuit on a simulator (or real hardware queue) is the fastest way to build quantum intuition beyond the math.
key_facts: A qubit's state is a superposition described by complex amplitudes, not a classical 0/1.
Gate-based circuits are the dominant programming model for near-term quantum hardware.
Simulators let you validate a circuit's logic before spending time on a real-hardware queue.
quantum_computing.exercise_idea: Build and simulate a Bell-state circuit in Qiskit and verify the expected entangled measurement distribution.

quantum_computing.title: Quantum Error Correction Basics
quantum_computing.rationale: Qubits decohere quickly, and error correction is the main obstacle between today's noisy hardware and fault-tolerant quantum computing.
key_facts: Physical qubits are noisy; logical qubits are encoded across many physical qubits for redundancy.
The surface code is the most widely pursued near-term error-correction scheme.
Error rates below a hardware-specific threshold are required before correction actually helps.
quantum_computing.exercise_idea: Simulate a simple 3-qubit bit-flip code and show it corrects a single injected error.

quantum_computing.title: Variational Algorithms QAOA and VQE
quantum_computing.rationale: Variational algorithms are the most practical near-term use of noisy quantum hardware, combining a quantum circuit with classical optimization.
key_facts: QAOA targets combinatorial optimization problems; VQE targets finding a molecule's ground-state energy.
Both alternate between a quantum circuit evaluation and a classical optimizer step.
Circuit depth is the main practical limit on near-term hardware for these algorithms.
quantum_computing.exercise_idea: Implement a small QAOA circuit for a toy Max-Cut problem and compare its result to the brute-force optimum.

quantum_computing.title: Quantum-Safe Cryptography Migration
quantum_computing.rationale: A sufficiently large fault-tolerant quantum computer would break RSA/ECC, making post-quantum cryptography migration a live infrastructure concern today.
key_facts: NIST has standardized post-quantum algorithms (e.g. CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium).
'Harvest now, decrypt later' attacks mean migration urgency exists even before large quantum computers do.
Hybrid classical+post-quantum schemes are the recommended near-term migration path.
quantum_computing.exercise_idea: Use a post-quantum cryptography library to generate a Kyber keypair and perform a key encapsulation round-trip.

quantum_computing.title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Workflows
quantum_computing.rationale: Nearly every practical near-term quantum application is a hybrid workflow, with the quantum step handling only the part classical computing can't do efficiently.
key_facts: Classical pre/post-processing usually dominates the wall-clock time of a hybrid workflow.
Result mitigation (error mitigation, not correction) is commonly applied classically to noisy quantum output.
Designing the classical/quantum split well is often more impactful than the quantum circuit itself.
quantum_computing.exercise_idea: Wrap a simulated quantum circuit call in a classical pre-processing/post-processing pipeline and document the split.
